correctness.summary: Stack buffer overflow when the base polynomial's degree is >= the modulus polynomial's degree (lenPoly close to or larger than lenModPoly). The base/temp/q/r buffers are sized `lenModPoly*2+1`, but the base polynomial is copied in and squared at its original (unreduced) length `lenPoly` before any reduction, so ToomCook writes `2*lenPoly-1` entries into `temp` (size lenModPoly*2+1) and copies lenPoly entries into `basePoly` (same size).
correctness.triggeringInput: poly = degree-4 polynomial, lenPoly=5 (e.g. {1,0,0,0,1} = x^4+1), modPoly = degree-2, lenModPoly=3 (e.g. {1,0,1} = x^2+1), exponent=3, any MOD. basePoly is stackalloc long[3*2+1=7] and lenBase=lenPoly=5; the first squaring ToomCook.Multiply(basePoly,5,basePoly,5,temp) writes 2*5-1=9 entries into temp of size 7 -> out-of-bounds write.
correctness.rootCause: The initial base polynomial is never reduced modulo modPoly before entering the square-and-multiply loop, and the buffers are sized assuming the base is already reduced (degree < deg modPoly). Computing p(x)^e mod m(x) with deg p >= deg m is a valid contract, so this overflows for representable inputs.
correctness.suggestedFix: Reduce the base modulo modPoly before the loop: run DivMod.Run(poly, lenPoly, modPoly, lenModPoly, ...) into basePoly so lenBase < lenModPoly, then size buffers as lenModPoly*2+1 (which is then sufficient). Alternatively size the temp/base buffers to max(lenPoly, lenModPoly*2+1).

perf.summary: Skip the final redundant base-squaring after the top exponent bit is consumed.
perf.currentCost: The loop unconditionally squares basePoly (ToomCook.Multiply + ComputeEffectiveLength + DivMod.Run) every iteration including the last, after the highest set bit has already been multiplied into result. That final square-and-reduce is a full polynomial multiply + division whose output is never used.
perf.proposedChange: Guard the squaring step: after exponent >>= 1, only square if exponent > 0L. e.g. exponent >>= 1; if (exponent == 0L) break; before the basePoly self-multiply, or move the squaring to the top of the next iteration. Equivalent: restructure to multiply-into-result first, test/shift, break when exponent hits 0, square only when more bits remain.
perf.rationale: Eliminates one of the most expensive operations in the whole routine (a ToomCook multiply plus a polynomial DivMod) on every PowMod call. For exponents with the top bit anywhere, the last square is pure waste; this is a guaranteed full-multiply saving per call.
perf.risk: Must ensure result has already absorbed the final bit before breaking. The odd-bit multiply happens at loop top using current basePoly, so breaking after the shift when exponent==0 is safe and preserves output exactly. No semantic change for any exponent >= 1.

perf.summary: Reuse a single scratch buffer instead of separate q and temp where lifetimes do not overlap.
perf.currentCost: Four stackalloc buffers of (lenModPoly*2+1) longs each: basePoly, q, r, temp. q and temp are both transient scratch within each step; q holds a quotient that is discarded immediately (only r is used as the reduced result).
perf.proposedChange: Since the quotient q is never read after DivMod (only r feeds back), q and temp can share storage if DivMod does not need them simultaneously distinct — but DivMod.Run takes temp(dividend), q(quotient out), r(remainder out) concurrently, so they must be distinct during the call. Keep distinct. Instead, narrow buffer sizing: temp only needs lenResult+lenBase-1 and lenBase+lenBase-1 worst cases, both <= 2*lenModPoly-1, so size 2*lenModPoly (drop the +1) is sufficient — saves 4 longs total and is clearer.
perf.rationale: Minor stack reduction on a hot recursive-ish routine; the main value is correct tight sizing on mobile stack.
perf.risk: Confirm DivMod/ToomCook never write the +1 guard slot. If any writes the index 2*lenModPoly (e.g., a degree-2k product term), the +1 is load-bearing — in that case leave as-is. Low confidence without ToomCook output-length contract; flag rather than apply blindly.

perf.summary: ComputeEffectiveLength after every multiply scans from the top for trailing zeros; pass the known exact product length to avoid the scan when no reduction needed.
perf.currentCost: After each ToomCook.Multiply the code calls ComputeEffectiveLength over the full product span (lenResult+lenBase-1), a backward scan that in the common dense case finds no leading zeros and walks at most a few elements, but is invoked twice per loop iteration.
perf.proposedChange: If ToomCook guarantees a normalized (no trailing-zero high coefficient) product for nonzero operands, the trim is unnecessary and the exact length lenResult+lenBase-1 can be used directly. Otherwise keep it. Confirm ToomCook's normalization contract.
perf.rationale: Removes a redundant O(degree) trailing-zero scan per multiply when the product is structurally dense (high coeff = product of two nonzero leading coeffs mod MOD, which is nonzero unless a zero-divisor arises mod composite MOD).
perf.risk: Mod a composite MOD, leading-coeff product can be 0 even with nonzero factors, so trimming IS needed there. Only safe to drop when MOD is prime. Since MOD is a runtime int (possibly composite), keep the trim. Reject for general MOD; viable only behind a prime-MOD precondition.
